[2] Basic analysis and visualization

[2.1] Functions to calculate the following metrics

– modified from those in the chytrid analysis

  • infestation_ratio, the ratio of the trees with herbivory)
  • average adult number (ave_basic), the total number of adults divided by the whole tree number
  • average herbivory impact (average_impact), the total number of adults divided by the number of trees with herbivory
  • deviation from Poisson distribution
  • standardized morisita index
#########new function at 2022/04/06: preparation for kibanA2023##############
spatial_distr_simple <- function(data0, title = "green", x_max = 10, LOG = F, drawing = FALSE) {
 
  # basic statistics
  ave_basic <- ave(data0)
  var_basic <- var(data0)
  cv_basic <- sqrt(var_basic)/ave_basic
  
  # Convert raw data into frequency distribution
  cut_test <- cut(data0, breaks = seq(-1, max(data0), by = 1))
  freq_dist <- as.data.frame(table(cut_test))
  
  infestation_ratio <- 1 - freq_dist$Freq[1] / sum(freq_dist$Freq)
  
  # delete long tail with NA
  data <- subset(freq_dist$Freq, complete.cases(freq_dist$Freq))
  # infestations
  infestations = 0:(length(data) - 1)
  # observed
  observed = c(data)
  total = sum(observed)
  
  # See the estimation of lamda http://www.singularpoint.org/blog/math/stat/cramer-rao-2/
  # https://www.statlect.com/fundamentals-of-statistics/Poisson-distribution-maximum-likelihood
  
  lambda = sum(infestations * observed) / total
  
  average_impact = sum(infestations * observed) / (total - observed[1])

  expected = total * ((lambda ^ infestations) * exp(-lambda)) / factorial(infestations)
  chi.squared = (observed - expected) ^ 2 / expected
  chi.squared.statistic = sum(chi.squared)
  
  #P Value for the Poisson distribution
  #https://web.stanford.edu/class/psych252/cheatsheets/chisquare.html
  P_chisq_Poission <- pchisq(chi.squared.statistic, length(observed) - 2, lower.tail = F)
  
  xmax <- x_max
  
  if(drawing == TRUE) {
    if(LOG == T) {
      plot(infestations, log10(observed), xlim = c(0,xmax), ylim = c(-0,3), cex = 3, pch = 16, cex.axis = 2, main = title)
      lines(infestations, log10(expected), col = 1,cex = 2, lwd = 3, lty = 2) #pure Poisson
    }
    else {
      plot(infestations, observed, xlim = c(0, xmax), cex = 3, ylim = c(0, max(observed + 10)), main = title)
      lines(infestations, expected, col = 1, cex = 2, lwd = 3,lty = 2) #pure Poisson
    }
  }
  
  morisita <- dispindmorisita(data0, unique.rm = FALSE, crit = 0.05)
  
  #imst is the standardized Morisita index: (-0.5:0.5) are confidence interval for random distribution
  cat("The ratio of infestations among trees is:", infestation_ratio, "\n")
  cat("The averaged number of infestations per tree is:", lambda, "\n")
  cat("The averaged number of infestations per infested tree is:", average_impact, "\n")
  cat("The probability with which Poisson distribution generates more extreme deviation:", P_chisq_Poission, "\n")
  cat("The CV is :", cv_basic[1], "\n")
  cat("The standardized morisita index value is :", morisita$imst, "\n")
  
  # return dataframe
  results_df <- data.frame(infestation_ratio, av_pop = lambda, av_impact = average_impact, smi = morisita$imst)
  return(results_df)
  
}

– specific growth rate

specific_growth <- function(value_vec, time_vec, tau = 1) {
  vec_length <- length(value_vec)
  growth <- numeric(vec_length)
  
  for(j in 1:vec_length) {
    if(j + tau - 1 < 1 || j + tau > vec_length) growth[j] <- NA
    else {
      growth[j] <- log(value_vec[j + tau] / value_vec[j + tau - 1]) / (time_vec[j + tau] - time_vec[j + tau - 1])
      if(value_vec[j + tau] == 0 & value_vec[j + tau - 1] == 0) growth[j] <- 0 #exception
    }
    if(is.infinite(growth[j])) growth[j] <- NA
  }
  # Noting that the value is not calculated at the final time point
  return(growth)
}

  • Codes for animation
# setting the max and min for color gradient
adult_min <- 0
adult_max <- 10

base_plot <- ggplot(adult_time_space, aes(x = X, y = Y, fill = adult)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "blue", limits = c(adult_min, adult_max)) +
  labs(title = "Leaf Beetle adult distributions",
       x = "Axis from North to South",
       y = "Axis from West to East",
       fill = "Adult") + coord_fixed(ratio = 3.0) +  
  theme_minimal()

animation <- base_plot +
  transition_time(time) +
  labs(title = "LB adult: Time {frame_time}")

set.seed(1234)
res_sadie <- list()
for(i in 1:length(unique(adult_time_space$time))) {
  cat("+")
  data_sub <- subset(adult_time_space, time == i)
  count_data_sub <- epiphy::count(data_sub, mapping(x = X, y = Y, t = time, i = adult))
  if(sum(count_data_sub$data$adult) < 1) next
  capture.output(res_sadie[[i]] <- sadie(count_data_sub, index = "all", threads = 2))
}

[4.2] Moran’s I calculation for all time steps (for loop)

res_moran <- list()
max_dist <- 3.0*sqrt(2) 
for(i in 1:length(unique(adult_time_space$time))) {
  cat("+")
  data_sub <- subset(adult_time_space, time == i)
  coords_sub <- cbind(data_sub$X, data_sub$Y) #extract coordinates
  nb_sub <- dnearneigh(coords_sub, 0, max_dist)
  lw_sub <- nb2listw(nb_sub, style = "W")
  if(sum(data_sub$adult) < 1) {
    res_moran[[i]] <- NA
    next
  }
  res_moran[[i]] <- moran.test(data_sub$adult, lw_sub)$statistic
}

– Candidate models were primarily evaluated based on predictive performance using rolling one-step-ahead forecasts over the final K time points. To account for small sample size and facilitate comparison from an information-theoretic perspective, AICc values were additionally computed and reported as a complementary criterion.

## 3) Fit all models by ML for calculating AICc using all time points
## =========================================================
fits_gls$pop_growth_1 <- lapply(candidate_formulas$pop_growth_1, function(fm) {
  try(
    gls(fm,
        data = beetle_summary_CAR1,
        correlation = corCAR1(form = ~ time),
        method = "ML", 
        na.action = na.omit),
    silent = TRUE
  )
})
#fits_gls$pop_growth_1

aicc <- sapply(fits_gls$pop_growth_1, AICc)
## =========================================================
## 4) Calculating RMSE by rolling 1-step ahead by the last K time points
## =========================================================
rolling_lastK_metrics <- function(df, forms, K,
                                  time_col = "time",
                                  y_col = "y",
                                  min_train = 10) {

  #cor_struct <- corCAR1(form = as.formula(paste0("~", time_col)))
  df <- df[order(df[[time_col]]), ]
  n <- nrow(df)
  stopifnot(n >= (min_train + K))

  start <- n - K

  eval_one <- function(form) {
    preds <- rep(NA_real_, n)

    for (t0 in start:(n - 1)) {
      train <- df[1:t0, , drop = FALSE]
      test  <- df[t0 + 1, , drop = FALSE]

      fit <- try(gls(form, data = train,
                     correlation = corCAR1(form = ~ time),
                     method = "ML",
                     na.action = na.omit),
                 silent = TRUE)
      if (inherits(fit, "try-error")) next

      pr <- try(as.numeric(predict(fit, newdata = test)), silent = TRUE)
      if (inherits(pr, "try-error")) next

      preds[t0 + 1] <- pr
    }

    ok <- !is.na(preds) & !is.na(df[[y_col]])
    e <- df[[y_col]][ok] - preds[ok]
    data.frame(
      RMSE = sqrt(mean(e^2, na.rm = TRUE)),
      MAE  = mean(abs(e), na.rm = TRUE),
      n_test = sum(ok), 
      pred1 = preds[start + 1], # specific for K = 6
      pred2 = preds[start + 2], 
      pred3 = preds[start + 3],
      pred4 = preds[start + 4],
      pred5 = preds[start + 5], 
      pred6 = preds[start + 6],
      e1 = abs(e[1]), # specific for K = 6
      e2 = abs(e[2]),
      e3 = abs(e[3]),
      e4 = abs(e[4]),
      e5 = abs(e[5]),
      e6 = abs(e[6]),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
    
  }

  res_list <- lapply(forms, eval_one)
  # summarizing into dataframe
  out <- do.call(rbind, res_list)
  out$model <- names(forms)
  out <- out[, c("model", "n_test", "RMSE", "MAE", "pred1", "pred2", "pred3", "pred4", "pred5", "pred6", "e1", "e2", "e3", "e4", "e5", "e6")]
  #out
}
results_temp <- rolling_lastK_metrics(
  df = beetle_summary_CAR1, 
  forms = candidate_formulas$pop_growth_1,
  K = 6, 
  time_col = "time", 
  y_col = "pop_growth_1"
  )

)

Visualization 03
  • Comparing the observed states and the forecasted from the rate for each of 6 final time points
time_length <- 27
beetle_compare <- beetle_summary[1:time_length, c("time", "av_pop", "infestation_ratio")]

beetle_compare$pop_pred_best <- rep(NA, time_length)
beetle_compare$pop_pred_alt <- rep(NA, time_length)
beetle_compare$pop_pred_base <- rep(NA, time_length)

#model choice 
best_model <- 1
alt_model <- 2
base_model <- 12

#specific for K = 6
K = 6
#starting point, identical to observation
beetle_compare$pop_pred_best[time_length - K] <- beetle_compare[time_length - K, "av_pop"]
beetle_compare$pop_pred_alt[time_length - K] <- beetle_compare[time_length - K, "av_pop"]
beetle_compare$pop_pred_base[time_length - K] <- beetle_compare[time_length - K, "av_pop"]
 
for(j in 1:6) {
  # time period
  delta_t <- beetle_compare[time_length - K + j, "time"] - beetle_compare[time_length - K + (j - 1), "time"]
  beetle_compare$pop_pred_best[time_length - K + j] <- beetle_compare[time_length - K + (j - 1), "av_pop"] * exp(results_table$pop_growth_1[best_model, 6 + j] * delta_t)
  beetle_compare$pop_pred_alt[time_length - K + j] <- beetle_compare[time_length - K + (j - 1), "av_pop"] * exp(results_table$pop_growth_1[alt_model, 6 + j] * delta_t)
  beetle_compare$pop_pred_base[time_length - K + j] <- beetle_compare[time_length - K + (j - 1), "av_pop"] * exp(results_table$pop_growth_1[base_model, 6 + j] * delta_t)
}

## =========================================================
## 2) DEFINE CANDIDATE MODELS (all subsets)
## =========================================================
# Model list as formulas; includes intercept-only baseline
candidate_formulas$prev_growth_1 <- list(
  m0 = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ 1"),
  m_pop = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ av_pop"),
  m_prev = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ infestation_ratio"),
  m_mi = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ smi"),
  m_LMX = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ LMX"),
  m_moran = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ moran"),
  m_pop_prev = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ av_pop + infestation_ratio"),
  m_pop_mi = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ av_pop + smi"),
  m_pop_LMX = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ av_pop + LMX"),
  m_pop_moran = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ av_pop + moran"),
  m_prev_mi = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ infestation_ratio + smi"),
  m_prev_LMX = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ infestation_ratio + LMX"),
  m_prev_LMX = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ infestation_ratio + moran"),
  m_mi_LMX = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ smi + LMX"),
  m_mi_moran = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ smi + moran"),
  m_moran_LMX = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ moran + LMX"),
  m_pop_prev_mi = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ av_pop + infestation_ratio + smi"),
  m_pop_prev_LMX = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ av_pop + infestation_ratio + LMX"),
  m_pop_prev_moran = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ av_pop + infestation_ratio + moran"),
  m_pop_mi_LMX = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ av_pop + smi + LMX"),
  m_prev_mi_LMX = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ infestation_ratio + smi + LMX"),
  m_pop_mi_moran = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ av_pop + smi + moran"),
  m_prev_mi_moran = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ infestation_ratio + smi + moran"),
  m_pop_moran_LMX = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ av_pop + moran + LMX"),
  m_prev_moran_LMX = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ infestation_ratio + moran + LMX"),
  m_mi_moran_LMX = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ smi + moran + LMX"),
  m_pop_prev_mi_LMX = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ av_pop + infestation_ratio + smi + LMX"),
  m_pop_prev_mi_moran = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ av_pop + infestation_ratio + smi + moran"),
  m_pop_prev_LMX_moran = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ av_pop + infestation_ratio + LMX + moran"),
  m_pop_mi_LMX_moran = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ av_pop + smi + LMX + moran"),
  m_prev_mi_LMX_moran = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ infestation_ratio + smi + LMX + moran"),
  m_all = as.formula("prev_growth_1 ~ av_pop + infestation_ratio + smi + LMX + moran")
)

– Candidate models were primarily ranked using AICc to account for small sample size. As a complementary assessment of predictive ability, model performance was additionally evaluated using rolling one-step-ahead forecasts over the final K time points.

## =========================================================
## 3) Fit all models by ML for calculating AICc using all time points
## =========================================================
fits_gls$prev_growth_1 <- lapply(candidate_formulas$prev_growth_1, function(fm) {
  try(
    gls(fm,
        data = beetle_summary_CAR1,
        correlation = corCAR1(form = ~ time),
        method = "ML",
        na.action = na.omit),
    silent = TRUE
  )
})
#fits_gls$pop_growth_1

aicc_prev <- sapply(fits_gls$prev_growth_1, AICc)
## =========================================================
## 4) Calculating RMSE by rolloing 1-step ahead by the last K time points
## =========================================================

results_temp_prev <- rolling_lastK_metrics(
  df = beetle_summary_CAR1, 
  forms = candidate_formulas$prev_growth_1,
  K = 6, 
  time_col = "time", 
  y_col = "prev_growth_1"
  )
print(results_temp_prev)

## =========================================================

results_table$prev_growth_1 <- data.frame(
  model = results_temp_prev$model,
  n_test = results_temp_prev$n_test,
  RMSE = results_temp_prev$RMSE,
  MAE = results_temp_prev$MAE,
  AICc = aicc_prev,
  delta = aicc_prev - min(aicc_prev),
  results_temp_prev[, -c(1:4)]   #for errors
)

results_table$prev_growth_1 <- results_table$prev_growth_1[order(results_table$prev_growth_1$RMSE), ]
print(results_table$prev_growth_1)
## =========================================================
## 6) FINAL REFIT: refit the selected structure on ALL data by REML

  • Comparing the error for each of 6 final time points
b <- results_table$prev_growth_1[14, -c(1:12)]  # only macro
best <- results_table$prev_growth_1[1, -c(1:12)] # best model (mi)
alt  <- results_table$prev_growth_1[2, -c(1:12)] # alternative model (moran)

b_minus_best <- b - best
b_minus_alt <- b - alt

# converting long format
rep_name <- c("t = 154", "t = 219", "t = 226", "t = 723", "t = 730", "t = 747")
df_delta <- rbind(
  data.frame(rep = rep_name, del_RMSE = unlist(b_minus_best[1, ]), model = "Best"),
  data.frame(rep = rep_name, del_RMSE = unlist(b_minus_alt[1, ]), model = "Alt_space")
)
ggplot(df_delta, aes(x = rep, y = del_RMSE, group = model)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  geom_point(aes(size = 3, color = model), alpha = 0.85, position = position_dodge(width = 0.4)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Best" = "#1b9e77",
                                "Alt_space" = "#d95f02"),
                     name = "Model") +
  labs(x = "forecasting point", y = expression(Delta*error == error[macro_only] - error[model]),
       title = "Leaf beetle prev:Per-point improvement") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1),
        aspect.ratio = 0.65
        )

Visualization 03
  • Comparing the observed states and the predicted from the rate for each of 6 final time points
beetle_compare$prev_pred_best <- rep(NA, time_length)
beetle_compare$prev_pred_alt <- rep(NA, time_length)
beetle_compare$prev_pred_base <- rep(NA, time_length)

#model choice 
best_model <- 1
alt_model <- 2
base_model <- 14

#specific for K = 6
K = 6
#starting point, identical to observation
beetle_compare$prev_pred_best[time_length - K] <- beetle_compare[time_length - K, "infestation_ratio"]
beetle_compare$prev_pred_alt[time_length - K] <- beetle_compare[time_length - K, "infestation_ratio"]
beetle_compare$prev_pred_base[time_length - K] <- beetle_compare[time_length - K, "infestation_ratio"]
 
for(j in 1:6) {
  # time period
  delta_t <- beetle_compare[time_length - K + j, "time"] - beetle_compare[time_length - K + (j - 1), "time"]
  beetle_compare$prev_pred_best[time_length - K + j] <- beetle_compare[time_length - K + (j - 1), "infestation_ratio"] * exp(results_table$prev_growth_1[best_model, 6 + j] * delta_t)
  beetle_compare$prev_pred_alt[time_length - K + j] <- beetle_compare[time_length - K + (j - 1), "infestation_ratio"] * exp(results_table$prev_growth_1[alt_model, 6 + j] * delta_t)
  beetle_compare$prev_pred_base[time_length - K + j] <- beetle_compare[time_length - K + (j - 1), "infestation_ratio"] * exp(results_table$prev_growth_1[base_model, 6 + j] * delta_t)
}

  geom_point(aes(y = prev_pred_best,
                 shape = "pred_best (mi): RMSE = 0.04514713"),
             color = "#1b9e77",
             size = 3) +
  
  geom_line(aes(y = prev_pred_alt,
                linetype = "prev_pred_alt"), color = "#d95f02") +
  geom_point(aes(y = prev_pred_alt,
                 shape = "pred_alt (moran): RMSE = 0.04856878"),
             color = "#d95f02",
             size = 3) +
  
  # pop_pred_base: dashed line + filled circle
  geom_line(aes(y = prev_pred_base,
                linetype = "prev_pred_macro_only"), color = "black") +
  geom_point(aes(y = prev_pred_base,
                 shape = "pred_macro_only (prev): RMSE = 0.08294828"),
             color = "black",
             size = 3) +

  # av_pop: solid line + filled rectangle
  geom_line(aes(y = infestation_ratio, linetype = "observed"), color = "black") +
  geom_point(aes(y = infestation_ratio, shape = "observed"),

    values = c(

    )
  ) +

  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c(
      "observed" = 15,               # filled rectangle (largest)

      "pred_alt (moran): RMSE = 0.04856878" = 18,     # filled diamond
      "pred_macro_only (prev): RMSE = 0.08294828" = 1     # open circle
    )
  ) +
  
  scale_x_continuous(
    name = "Time (hours)",
  ) +
  
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Prevalence (infestation ratio)",

    shape = NULL

– Save some objects for the manuscript

beetle_prev_growth_model <- best_formula$prev_growth_1
beetle_popl_growth_fitted <- final_fit$pop_growth_1
beetle_prev_growth_fitted <- final_fit$prev_growth_1

save(
  beetle_popl_growth_model, 
  beetle_prev_growth_model, 
  beetle_popl_growth_fitted, 
  beetle_prev_growth_fitted, 
  file = "beetle_bestfit.RData")
